topic: Higher Order Derivatives: Unveiling Rates of Change of Rates

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The First Derivative
lecture_lines: The first derivative is a rate of change.
It measures the slope of the tangent line.
animations: Show function f(x) and its tangent slope at point x. Color: #FFFFFF. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png]
Animate tangent slope changing value as x increases. Color: #FF00FF.
Label the slope as f'(x) on the graph. Color: #00FFFF.

sections.title: Defining Higher Order Derivatives
lecture_lines: Higher order derivatives are derivatives of derivatives.
We differentiate a function multiple times.
Second derivative f double prime measures concavity. [Asset: concavity_viz]
animations: Define f''(x) as the derivative of f'(x). Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate the second derivative operation visually. Color: #FF00FF.

sections.title: Physical Interpretation: Acceleration
lecture_lines: In physics, first derivative is velocity.
G-force relates to the second derivative. [Asset: accel_viz]
animations: Show a car moving with increasing velocity using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png]. Color: #FFFFFF.
Plot position s(t) and its tangent slope. Color: #FF00FF.
Label slope as velocity v(t) = s'(t). Color: #00FFFF.

sections.title: Computational Step-by-Step
lecture_lines: Differentiate powers repeatedly using the power rule.
Function f of x equals x to fourth.
First derivative is four x cubed.
Second derivative is twelve x squared. [Asset: power_rule_viz]
animations: Apply power rule again: d/dx(4x^3) = 12x^2. Color: #00FFFF.

sections.title: Summary and Intuition
lecture_lines: Derivatives quantify how curvy functions are.
Example: Roller coaster jerk feeling. [Asset: coaster_viz]
animations: Display hierarchy: position, velocity, acceleration. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate the connection between each layer. Color: #FF00FF.
